result:
I found 11 rules whose behavior didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`. I also fixed rule 47, whose behavior didn't need changing. After the fixes, all 150 rules give the same results as a reference built straight from the docstrings.

**Rules that behaved differently (11)**
| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | Discount was rounded with `round()`, breaking the rule that discounts are floored to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 45 | The 10,000-won cap was applied to the amount before the percentage, not to the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 46 | `qty > 100`, so exactly 100 units got no discount | `qty >= 100` |
| 69 | Discount was 13%; the docstring says 12% | Changed to 12% |
| 90 | The 100,000-won cap was applied to the base price, not the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 100 | A "whole" rule was calculating the discount only on units above the threshold (marginal) | Changed to `base * 12 // 100` |
| 114 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 200,000 won | Always cap at 100,000 won |
| 123 | `qty > 100`, so exactly 100 units got no discount | `qty >= 100` |
| 136 | A "whole" rule was calculated as marginal | Changed to `base * 15 // 100` |
| 144 | A "marginal" rule was calculated as whole | Changed to `(qty - 20) * unit * 12 // 100` |
| 150 | The 10,000-won cap was applied to the base price, not the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |

**Changed to match the docstring's wording only:** rule 47 used `qty > 50`, while the docstring says "50+ units". Since it's a marginal rule, the discount at exactly 50 units is 0 either way, so the results don't change. I changed it to `qty >= 50` anyway.

**How I checked:** I wrote a script that reads all 150 docstrings and builds a reference calculation from them, following the module docstring's general rules. The order is: threshold check, whole or marginal, percentage, floor to the won, then cap the discount. Before the fixes, it found the 11 rules above. After the fixes, all 150 rules gave the same results as the reference. The test used quantities 0–129 plus several large values, with 14 unit prices that included 0 and odd numbers. It also confirmed that negative inputs still raise `ValueError`. A copy of the original file is saved as `pricebook.orig.py` in the scratchpad folder.

STATUS: DONE
